entry:gpai-cop:cov.note: All nine coverage elements are supported, timing included (trigger points in the Framework, full assessment before placing on the market). Measure 4.1 tiers are capability-based, measurable and set by signatories; the 10^25 FLOP presumption is the Act's. Commitment 6 (legal text Art. 55(1)) and Appendices 4.2–4.5 cover unreleased parameters, interfaces, physical access, insider threats, external security reviews and red-teaming. Measure 5.1 lists filtering, refusals and staged access; marking falls under the separate Art. 50 code. Model Report updates go to the AI Office at least every six months; non-signatories must justify alternative compliance.

entry:eu-aia:cov.note: Each listed element has a textual basis in the current OJ text: thresh Art. 51(2); eval and elicit Art. 55(1)(a) (adversarial testing); timing Art. 72; sec Art. 55(1)(d); mit Arts. 5, 50(2); acct Art. 55(1)(c); halt Art. 93(1)(c); update Arts. 51(3), 56(8).

entry:eu-aia:cov:mit.note: Factual core verified: prohibited practices (Art. 5(1)), GPAI copyright policy (Art. 53(1)(c)), Art. 50(2) marking, systemic-risk mitigation (Art. 55(1)(b)). 'The most comprehensive deployment-mitigation regime in any binding instrument' is comparative.

entry:eu-aia:cov:acct.note: Incident reporting (Art. 55(1)(c)), access (Art. 92(3)), recall (Art. 93(1)(c)) and €15M/3% (Art. 101) verified, but the Digital Omnibus moved supervision of AI systems built on a provider's own GPAI model, and their high-risk incident reports, to the AI Office (new Art. 75(1), (1a)).

entry:eu-aia:cov:update.note: Codes reviewable (Art. 56(8)); delegated acts amend the thresholds (Art. 51(3)) and Annex III (Art. 7(1)); other changes need legislation (as the 2026 Omnibus itself shows).

gap:elicit.note: Factual core verified: the AI Act requires adversarial testing (Art. 55(1)(a)) but not elicitation by name; the GPAI Code explicitly requires state-of-the-art elicitation (Appendix 3.2) and is voluntary. 'Almost no statute requires it', where the work happens, and the counterfactual are analytic.

faq:what-does-the-eu-ai-act-require-for-.note: 10^25 presumption (Art. 51(2)); Art. 55(1)(a)-(d) list matches; Annex XI Section 2 covers evaluation strategies and adversarial testing; reliance on codes until harmonised standards (Art. 55(2)).

faq:what-does-the-eu-ai-office-do.note: Verified: established by Commission Decision of 24 Jan 2024 within DG CNECT; enforces GPAI rules (Art. 88(1)); model access (Art. 92(3)), recall (Art. 93(1)(c)), €15M/3% fines (Art. 101); Art. 101 applies from 2 Aug 2026 (Art. 113(b)). 'Runs the Scientific Panel' is loose (the Office provides its secretariat/administrative support; the Panel advises the Office). 'A centralised role unique within EU regulatory architecture' is comparative.
